newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq starting Mina al-Bakr oil export operations.
newsitem.headline: Iraq starting Mina al-Bakr oil export operations.

text.p: Iraq was expected on Monday to resume exports from its Mina al-Bakr terminal on the Gulf under the second phase of the oil-for-food deal monitored by the United Nations, the ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra reported.
"Operations of Iraq crude exports via Mina al-Bakr port will be resumed today after two months' suspension," the paper said.

The Iraqi news agency INA quoted the director-general of the Iraqi Southern Oil Company, Abdul-Bari Mahmoud, as saying the very large crude carrier (VLCC) Stena Companion chartered by U.S. Coastal Corp was expected to dock at the port on Monday afternoon.
The Jahre Ventura, originally scheduled to load first, was now due to arrive on Tuesday to take 2.5 million barrels for U.S. trader Bayoil, Mahmoud said.
Iraq resumed limited oil exports under the second phase of the U.N. agreement last Wednesday from the Turkish port of Ceyhan.
Three tankers, the Arcadia (Bayoil), New Horizon (Coastal) and the Landsort (Total ) have so far exported cargoes of Iraq's Kirkuk crude from Ceyhan.

The pact allows Iraq to sell $2 billlion worth of oil over six months in two equal 90-day instalments and was renewed for a second phase on June 8. Iraq has delayed exports to modify plans for aid distribution.
